chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, 'Ali, Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, ordered Qanbar to administer a hadd punishment to a man, but Qanbar erred and gave him three lashes more than eighty. So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام exacted retribution from Qanbar, and Qanbar was flogged three lashes.

key_terms.أَسْوَاطٍ: lashes or strokes of the whip
key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ: eighty, the prescribed number of lashes referenced in the report
key_terms.حَدًّا: a fixed legal punishment prescribed by the sacred law
key_terms.غَلِطَ: made an error in carrying out the punishment
key_terms.فَأَقَادَهُ: he exacted retaliation or legal requital from him
key_terms.قَنْبَرَ: Qanbar, the servant of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام tasked with carrying out the punishment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam 'Ali عليه السلام do when Qanbar exceeded the prescribed hadd punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith shows that Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام enforced justice even in the execution of prescribed punishments, holding the enforcer accountable for exceeding the lawful limit. It highlights the principle that unlawful excess in punishment is itself subject to retribution.
